[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Ship Combat[/color][/head]
Ship weapons can destroy vessels, stations, and other players with little warning. Confirm your target, chain of command, and the [textlink="Roleplay Rules" link="RoleplayRules"] before firing. In-world hostility never overrides server rules.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Turrets and targeting consoles[/color][/head]
Turret weapons are mounted in hardpoints and controlled through a targeting console. Select the intended weapon or weapon group, verify its ammunition and readiness, then select a target on the tactical display. Selected weapons are highlighted on your ship's IFF display.
[bold]IFF[/bold] means Identification Friend or Foe. It helps identify contacts, but it is not permission to fire: ships can be unregistered, captured, disguised, or incorrectly identified. Confirm important contacts over radio when possible.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Fixed weapons[/color][/head]
Fixed weapons face with the hull and may be controlled by the shuttle console or linked controls. They trade turret coverage for direct forward fire. Before combat, confirm their power, ammunition, firing arc, and control method; never discover these details while approaching a friendly dock.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Hardpoints[/color][/head]
Hardpoints connect compatible turret weapons to the ship. Their size and weapon type limit what can be installed. Most are part of the hull and cannot simply be moved between ships, so ask an experienced engineer before removing or replacing a turret.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Shields and power[/color][/head]
Deflector emitters use ship power to stop projectiles and explosions. A damaged shield consumes power while recovering; an overloaded or poorly supplied shield can starve thrusters, weapons, life support, or other systems. Watch the power grid and coordinate with engineering instead of repeatedly forcing a failing shield online.
[color=#8fc98a]Before leaving dock, assign a pilot, gunner, engineer, and radio channel. A crew that communicates is more dangerous and much less likely to shoot the wrong target.[/color]
